issues.description: Ask for push permission at the moment it means something — after the first shift is visible, not on first launch — and let staff turn shift reminders on and off from settings.

comments.author: Amir Haddad
comments.body: Shipped in the 15 July staff-app release. Shift reminders are on by default once the first shift is visible.

issues.description: One encrypted store for third-party OAuth tokens — Fortnox first, Visma next — with refresh handling and per-tenant isolation, so every integration does not invent its own.

comments.author: Nils Ek
comments.body: Encryption and per-tenant isolation are in. Refresh-on-expiry is the piece left, and SCH-125 needs it before it can talk to a real Fortnox account.

issues.description: Nightly snapshot of every published schedule to object storage with 30-day retention, so a bad bulk edit on a chain's week can be rolled back instead of rebuilt by hand.
Approved hours from the schedule go to the customer's payroll system instead of being retyped. A CSV export first, then a direct Fortnox connector; Visma after that. Fortnox is the first target.

comments.author: Rebecca Holm
comments.body: The approved-hours CSV is out. The Fortnox connector is in progress and needs the platform token store before it can hold real customer credentials.

issues.description: Export approved hours for a period as CSV: person, location, date, hours, cost centre. One column set that both Fortnox and Visma accept, so the connectors later map from the same shape.

comments.author: Rebecca Holm
comments.body: Column set verified against a real Fortnox import template and a Visma one. Closing.

comments.author: Rebecca Holm
comments.body: Enabled for every chain in the 24 June release. Managers export from the period view.

issues.description: Push approved hours straight into Fortnox instead of handing the manager a file: OAuth against the customer's Fortnox account, locations mapped to cost centres, one push per period, and a readable report of what Fortnox rejected.

comments.author: Nils Ek
comments.body: Mapping and the push work against the Fortnox sandbox. Real customer accounts need somewhere to keep refresh tokens, which is PLT-77 — I am not putting them in this service.

issues.description: Staff propose a shift swap in the app, the affected colleague accepts, the manager approves, and the schedule updates for both people. Three stories: the swap request model and API, the request screen in the staff app, and the manager approval flow. Rules: same role, same location, manager approves, no overtime beyond contract.

comments.author: Rebecca Holm
comments.body: Scope agreed: same role, same location, manager approves, and a swap can never push either person past their contracted hours. Split into three stories.

comments.author: Rebecca Holm
comments.body: SCH-232 and SCH-236 are Done. SCH-240 is what is left, and the overtime check in it is bigger than the original estimate. Re-estimate before anyone quotes a date.

issues.description: A swap request as a first-class object: who proposes it, which shift, which colleague, and the state it is in (proposed, accepted by the colleague, approved, rejected). Plus the REST endpoints the staff app and the manager web both read and write.

comments.author: Rebecca Holm
comments.body: Endpoints are live behind the swaps flag, with same-role and same-location validation on the request itself. Closing.

issues.summary: Swap request screen in staff app
issues.description: The staff-app screen where someone picks one of their own shifts, picks a colleague who can work that role at that location, and sends the swap request. Includes the list of requests they have sent and received.

comments.author: Amir Haddad
comments.body: Shipped behind the swaps flag. The sent/received list reuses the shift list component, so nothing new to maintain. Closing.

issues.summary: Manager approval flow and schedule update
issues.description: The manager sees the week's pending swaps, approves or rejects each one, and an approval rewrites the schedule for both people. The approval must refuse anything that pushes either person past their contracted hours for the week.

comments.author: Rebecca Holm
comments.body: Approval list and the reject path work against the API. Starting on the schedule write.

comments.author: Rebecca Holm
comments.body: This needs a re-estimate. The overtime check has to run against both people's contracted hours for the whole week, not just the two shifts, and the week can already contain other approved swaps. I would rather re-estimate than give a date now.

pages.title: Roadmap H2
pages.body:
Roadmap H2

The order below is the plan of record. Q3 is July to September, Q4 is October to December. Anything not on this page is not committed, whatever anyone has been told.

Committed

First: payroll export (Fortnox first), in Q3.

Then: shift swaps, in Q4.

Both epics sit with the Scheduling team, which is why this is an order and not two dates: if one moves up, the other one moves a quarter.

Exploring

Auto-schedule suggestions. Suggest next week's schedule from last week plus stated availability, for the manager to edit rather than accept. No team, no date, and it stays that way until the swaps work is out.

Not doing

Offline mode in the staff app. Declined in February and again in May: back offices have wifi, and the app already caches the shifts a person needs to read.

pages.title: Product weekly update
pages.body:
Product weekly update

Published Friday, newest first. Three sentences per area; if something needs more than that it needs a meeting, not a paragraph.

2026-07-10

Shift swaps. Two of the three stories are done and the manager approval flow is the one left. The overtime check inside it is larger than estimated, so it is being re-estimated before anyone gives a date. Nothing on the page moves until that number exists.

Payroll export. The approved-hours CSV shipped on 2026-06-24 with a column set both Fortnox and Visma accept. The Fortnox connector works against the sandbox and is waiting on the platform token store.

2026-07-03

Payroll export. The approved-hours CSV is in review, one column set for both payroll systems rather than one per customer. The Fortnox connector starts next week.

Shift swaps. The request model and API are done and the staff-app screen is about a week out. Both epics are on the same team, so a change of order moves one of them a quarter; the capacity numbers are with the CPO.
